23 A sound wave of frequency 270 Hz is recorded by a cathode-ray oscilloscope (CRO).
The waveform on the CRO is shown.
1 cm
What is the time-base setting on the CRO?
A
0.1 ms cm–1
B
1 ms cm–1
C
10 ms cm–1
D
100 ms cm–1

hints: Count how many $\text{cm}$ in the horizontal direction correspond to one full cycle of the $270 \text{ Hz}$ sine wave on the CRO screen.
Recall that period $T = 1/f$ for the sound wave, so calculate $T$ in $\text{ms}$ from $f = 270 \text{ Hz}$.
Connect the two by time-base $= T$ divided by length of one cycle in $\text{cm}$, to get time per $\text{cm}$ in $\text{ms cm}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Find the period of the sound wave from its frequency: $T = 1/f = 1/270 \text{ Hz} \approx 0.00370 \text{ s} \approx 3.7 \text{ ms}$.
Measure one wavelength on the trace in the horizontal direction. From a rising zero-crossing to the next rising zero-crossing is about $4 \text{ cm}$, using the $1 \text{ cm}$ scale marker.
The time-base setting is time per distance: $\text{time-base} = \text{period} / \text{length of one cycle}$.
Substitute values with units: $\text{time-base} \approx 3.7 \text{ ms} / 4 \text{ cm} \approx 0.93 \text{ ms cm}^{-1}$.
This is closest to $1 \text{ ms cm}^{-1}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: This is 10 times too small. It would give a period of about $0.4 \text{ ms}$ for a $4 \text{ cm}$ wave, corresponding to about $2500 \text{ Hz}$.

B.explanation: A $270 \text{ Hz}$ wave has period about $3.7 \text{ ms}$ and one cycle spans about $4 \text{ cm}$, giving about $1 \text{ ms cm}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: This is 10 times too large. It would give a period of about $40 \text{ ms}$ for a $4 \text{ cm}$ wave, corresponding to only $25 \text{ Hz}$.

D.explanation: This is 100 times too large. It would give a period of about $400 \text{ ms}$ for a $4 \text{ cm}$ wave, corresponding to only $2.5 \text{ Hz}$.
